problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate a fixed budget across 18 different infrastructure projects to maximize the overall public benefit score.
The profile for each project is as follows:
* Project A: benefit score is 0.030, disruption index is 0.035, allocation bounds [0.090, 0.731]
* Project B: benefit score is 0.087, disruption index is 0.175, allocation bounds [0.050, 0.896]
* Project C: benefit score is 0.096, disruption index is 0.023, allocation bounds [0.050, 0.601]
* Project D: benefit score is 0.069, disruption index is 0.296, allocation bounds [0.078, 0.895]
* Project E: benefit score is 0.039, disruption index is 0.150, allocation bounds [0.002, 0.665]
* Project F: benefit score is 0.085, disruption index is 0.024, allocation bounds [0.080, 0.614]
* Project G: benefit score is 0.160, disruption index is 0.037, allocation bounds [0.048, 0.761]
* Project H: benefit score is 0.080, disruption index is 0.099, allocation bounds [0.087, 0.568]
* Project I: benefit score is 0.063, disruption index is 0.294, allocation bounds [0.004, 0.379]
* Project J: benefit score is 0.049, disruption index is 0.228, allocation bounds [0.016, 0.475]
* Project K: benefit score is 0.039, disruption index is 0.288, allocation bounds [0.068, 0.674]
* Project L: benefit score is 0.058, disruption index is 0.155, allocation bounds [0.008, 0.864]
* Project M: benefit score is 0.022, disruption index is 0.101, allocation bounds [0.063, 0.324]
* Project N: benefit score is 0.184, disruption index is 0.123, allocation bounds [0.095, 0.728]
* Project O: benefit score is 0.054, disruption index is 0.113, allocation bounds [0.023, 0.710]
* Project P: benefit score is 0.056, disruption index is 0.048, allocation bounds [0.022, 0.443]
* Project Q: benefit score is 0.187, disruption index is 0.206, allocation bounds [0.068, 0.898]
* Project R: benefit score is 0.063, disruption index is 0.106, allocation bounds [0.014, 0.664]
Each project must receive a fraction of the total budget that falls within its specified lower and upper bounds, and the sum of all budget fractions must equal one. To prioritize key initiatives, the planner requires that the group of core projects, represented by the subset L = {A, B, C, D, E, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, P, R}, collectively receive at least 0.694 of the total budget. Furthermore, the overall portfolio disruption index must not exceed 0.137, and the total public benefit score must be no less than 0.081. Please determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total public benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
